emb:L2029578380.model_family: machine learning models trained on functional connectivity profiles (algorithm not specified)
emb:L2029578380.clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive abilities (IQ, visuospatial, verbal comprehension, fluid reasoning) from resting-state functional connectivity in ADHD
emb:L2029578380.patient_population: children and adolescents ages 6-16 from the Healthy Brain Network, neurotypical (n=106) and ADHD (n=373)
emb:L2029578380.model_description: Functional connectivity profiles were generated from fMRI collected while children and adolescents watched a movie clip. Machine learning models were trained with out-of-sample cross-validation to predict IQ, visuospatial ability, verbal comprehension, and fluid reasoning from these connectivity patterns.
emb:L2029578380.release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
emb:L2029578380.headline_result: Models successfully predicted IQ, visuospatial, verbal comprehension, and fluid reasoning in children 6-11, but not in adolescents with ADHD (no quantitative metric stated).

emb:L2027952319.model_family: ensemble learning (balanced random forest, XGBoost, EasyEnsemble classifier) on graph-theoretical connectivity features
emb:L2027952319.clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of ADHD from audiovisual integration network connectivity on resting-state fMRI
emb:L2027952319.patient_population: children with ADHD versus neurotypical controls from the ADHD-200 resting-state fMRI dataset
emb:L2027952319.model_description: Resting-state fMRI from the ADHD-200 dataset was used to derive graph-theoretical features of auditory-visual integration network connectivity. Ensemble machine-learning classifiers (balanced random forest, XGBoost, EasyEnsemble) were trained to distinguish children with ADHD from neurotypical controls, with XGBoost giving the most balanced sensitivity and specificity.
emb:L2027952319.release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
emb:L2027952319.dataset_size: ADHD-200 resting-state fMRI dataset (exact n not stated)
emb:L2027952319.headline_result: Moderate diagnostic accuracy with balanced sensitivity and specificity for XGBoost (exact values not stated).

emb:L2026946495.model_family: machine learning classifier on structural MRI features; separate brain-age prediction model
emb:L2026946495.clinical_problem: classification of pubertal (pre- vs post-menarche) status and brain age estimation from structural brain MRI
emb:L2026946495.patient_population: age-matched adolescent females from the ABCD cohort
emb:L2026946495.model_description: Cortical and subcortical structural MRI from age-matched adolescent females in the ABCD cohort was used to train a machine-learning model that classifies pre- versus post-menarche status as a continuous class probability. A separately trained brain-age prediction model (from the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort) was applied to the same data to compute brain age gaps for comparison.
emb:L2026946495.release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
emb:L2026946495.dataset_size: age-matched adolescent females, ABCD cohort (exact n not stated)
emb:L2026946495.headline_result: Moderate but statistically significant accuracy in menarche classification (exact value not stated); menarche class probability, but not brain age gap, was associated with age at menarche.

emb:L2026946201.model_family: deep learning with automated feature selection, multimodal (including MRI-only variant)
emb:L2026946201.clinical_problem: prediction of onset of ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder, and conduct disorder from multimodal predictors including structural and functional brain MRI
emb:L2026946201.patient_population: children age 9-10 years from the ABCD cohort, followed to age 11-12
emb:L2026946201.model_description: 5,777 multimodal candidate predictors, including structural, functional, and diffusion brain MRI along with demographic and psychosocial data, were collected from 9-10 year olds in the ABCD cohort. A deep-learning model with an automated feature-selection algorithm was trained to predict future onset of ADHD, ODD, and CD at 2-year follow-up; a neuroimaging-only variant was also tested.
emb:L2026946201.release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
emb:L2026946201.dataset_size: 5,777 candidate predictors from the ABCD cohort, ages 9-10 (exact n not stated)
emb:L2026946201.headline_result: Multimodal models achieved ~86-97% accuracy and AUROC 0.919-0.996; MRI-only models achieved ~80% accuracy and AUROC.

emb:L2022983962.exclusion_reason: study population age not stated in abstract; cannot confirm an at-least-partly pediatric cohort

emb:L2025675651.model_family: deep learning: graph convolutional network with low-rank multimodal tensor fusion
emb:L2025675651.clinical_problem: ASD classification from cortical morphology (gray matter volume, cortical thickness, surface area) on structural MRI during early brain development
emb:L2025675651.patient_population: children with ASD compared to typically developing children during the early brain overgrowth period
emb:L2025675651.model_description: Structural MRI-derived cortical morphology metrics (gray matter volume, cortical thickness, surface area) from children with ASD and typically developing controls were used to characterize developmental trajectories. An end-to-end deep-learning model (LMFGCN) combining graph convolutional networks with intermediate low-rank multimodal tensor fusion was trained to classify ASD, outperforming early- and late-integration baselines.
emb:L2025675651.release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
emb:L2025675651.headline_result: LMFGCN outperformed early- and late-integration methods and other state-of-the-art models in ASD classification (exact metric not stated).

emb:L2018154832.model_family: connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM), a machine-learning regression approach on functional connectivity
emb:L2018154832.clinical_problem: prediction of transdiagnostic social impairment (SRS-2 score) from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity during movie-watching
emb:L2018154832.patient_population: transdiagnostic sample of youths with neurodevelopmental/psychiatric diagnoses (ASD, ADHD, mood, anxiety), mean age 11.68 years, from the Healthy Brain Network
emb:L2018154832.model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity was acquired during a social movie-watching task in a transdiagnostic youth sample. Connectome-based predictive modeling was trained via cross-validation to predict Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2) scores from connectivity data, with prediction confirmed in an independent replication sample.
emb:L2018154832.release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
emb:L2018154832.dataset_size: N=144 (transdiagnostic Healthy Brain Network sample); replication sample n=41
emb:L2018154832.headline_result: 10-fold cross-validation predicted SRS-2 (q2=0.32, r=0.57, p<.001); replicated in an independent sample (r=0.33, p<.035).
emb:L2018154832.study_design: retrospective machine-learning prediction study with independent replication

emb:L2017166847.model_family: multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) classifier on functional connectivity
emb:L2017166847.clinical_problem: classification of familial risk for developmental dyslexia from infant resting-state functional connectivity of the left fusiform gyrus
emb:L2017166847.patient_population: infants with (n=35) and without (n=63) a familial history of dyslexia, mean age ~8-9 months, recruited at Boston Children's Hospital
emb:L2017166847.model_description: Structural and resting-state functional MRI were acquired in infants with and without familial risk for dyslexia. Multivariate pattern analysis was trained to classify infants by familial risk status using whole-brain functional connectivity to 20 predefined language/reading regions; connectivity of the left fusiform gyrus gave the strongest discrimination.
emb:L2017166847.release_evidence: preprint with no stated code or product release
emb:L2017166847.headline_result: Classification accuracy 0.55 (p_corrected < 0.001, Cohen's d = 0.76) distinguishing familial risk status from left fusiform gyrus connectivity.

emb:L2017166020.model_family: machine learning (algorithm not specified) on structural MRI and DTI features
emb:L2017166020.clinical_problem: prediction of adolescent alcohol misuse from structural and diffusion brain MRI
emb:L2017166020.patient_population: adolescents assessed at ages 14, 19, and 22 from the IMAGEN cohort (n≈1182)
emb:L2017166020.model_description: T1-weighted structural and diffusion tensor imaging from adolescents at ages 14, 19, and 22 in the IMAGEN cohort were used to train a machine-learning model predicting adolescent alcohol misuse (AAM) at age 22, tested on independent data; earlier-age scans (14, 19) were also used to predict later AAM.
emb:L2017166020.release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
emb:L2017166020.headline_result: Balanced accuracy 78% predicting alcohol misuse at age 22 from age-22 brain structure; 73% and 75% using age-14 and age-19 data respectively.

emb:L2015873901.model_family: predictive modeling (train/test/held-out) using graph-theoretic global efficiency features from fMRI
emb:L2015873901.clinical_problem: prediction of irritability severity from task- and resting-state fMRI brain network global efficiency during and after a frustration task
emb:L2015873901.patient_population: transdiagnostic sample of 66 youths, mean age 14 years
emb:L2015873901.model_description: Task-based and resting-state fMRI were collected before, during, and after a frustration-inducing task in a transdiagnostic youth sample. A train/test/held-out predictive model used network global efficiency to predict self- and observer-rated irritability, identifying fronto-temporal-limbic and motor-parietal-subcortical networks as the most informative.
emb:L2015873901.release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
emb:L2015873901.headline_result: Post-task network global efficiency predicted self- and observer-rated irritability in held-out data (specific statistic not given).

emb:L2015549032.model_family: canonical correlation analysis (machine learning) on resting-state functional connectome
emb:L2015549032.clinical_problem: prediction of a combined cognitive-psychopathology dimension and psychiatric disorder risk from resting-state functional connectome in preadolescents
emb:L2015549032.patient_population: 11,875 youths aged 9-10 years at baseline from the ABCD study, followed over 2 years
emb:L2015549032.model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity from 9-10 year olds in the ABCD study was linked to multi-domain cognitive and psychopathology measures using a canonical-correlation-analysis-based machine-learning model, trained on 5,096 and tested on 1,476 held-out participants. The resulting connectome factor predicted diagnosis transitions over a 2-year follow-up and was highly heritable.
emb:L2015549032.release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
emb:L2015549032.headline_result: 5-fold cross-validation rho=0.68-0.73 (train) and 0.56-0.58 (test); heritability h2=74.42%; predicted diagnosis transitions over 2-year follow-up.

emb:L2014449305.model_family: machine learning with opportunistic stacking across multimodal MRI
emb:L2014449305.clinical_problem: prediction of childhood cognitive ability from multimodal brain MRI (task fMRI, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, DTI)
emb:L2014449305.patient_population: approximately 11,000 children from the ABCD cohort, followed over 2 years during early adolescence
emb:L2014449305.model_description: Multimodal MRI (task-based fMRI from three tasks, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, and DTI) from the ABCD cohort was combined using a machine-learning model with 'opportunistic stacking' to handle missing data. The model predicted cognitive ability scores, explaining about 20% of variance, remained stable across two years, and generalized across sites; predictions partially mediated associations with socio-demographic, psychological, and genetic factors.
emb:L2014449305.release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
emb:L2014449305.headline_result: Brain-based model explained ~20% of variance in childhood cognition, stable across 2 years and generalizable across sites.

emb:L2009014992.model_family: explainable machine learning; comparison of nine predictive algorithms including Elastic Net
emb:L2009014992.clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive ability measures from task-based (n-back working memory) fMRI in children
emb:L2009014992.patient_population: children from the ABCD cohort (n=3,989) performing an n-back working-memory task
emb:L2009014992.model_description: Task-based fMRI during an n-back working-memory task in children from the ABCD study was used to train and compare nine machine-learning algorithms (including Elastic Net) for out-of-sample prediction of 12 cognitive abilities. Explainability methods (SHAP, eNetXplorer, accumulated local effects, Friedman's H-statistic) were used to interpret which brain features drove the predictions.
emb:L2009014992.release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
emb:L2009014992.headline_result: Machine-learning algorithms, notably Elastic Net, outperformed mass-univariate and OLS regression in out-of-sample prediction of cognition (specific metric not given).
